1 بَهَأ بِهِ , and بَهِئَ, (AZ, S, Mgh, K,) [aor.
بَهَاَ ,] and بَهُؤَ, (K,) [aor.
بَهُاَ ] inf. n. بَهْءٌ and بُهُوْءٌ (AZ, S, K) and بَهَآءٌ; (K;) and به ↓ ابتهأ ; (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA;) He was, or became, sociable, friendly, or familiar, with him, or it; (AZ, S, Mgh, K;) namely, a man, (AZ, S,) or a thing; (Mgh;) and loved, or liked, his, or its, nearness: (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA:) and he became familiar with it so as to have little, or no, reverence for it, or awe of it. (Mgh, TA.) بَهَوْا بِهِ occurs in a trad., as they relate it, for بَهَؤُوا به: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) and ↓ يَبْتَهِى , in a verse of El-Aashà, for يَبْتَهِئُ. (As, O, TS, L.) ―
-b2- مَا بَهَأْتُ لَهُ I did not understand it; or I did not know it; (ISk, S, K;) as also مَا بَأَهْتُ لَهُ. (ISk, S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
